title: Transcriptomics and network pharmacology reveal that baicalin alleviates acute lung injury induced by H1N1 via targeting STAT1.
authors: He, Wenxiang; Dou, Yufeng; Ji, Hui; Li, Xia; Liang, Pengbo; Liu, Xiaoli
one_liner_zh: 该文研究黄芩苷通过STAT1缓解H1N1诱导的急性肺损伤，属于疾病机制与药物靶点研究，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Hemagglutinin 1 neuraminidase 1 (H1N1) infection triggers acute lung injury (ALI), and baicalin exerts therapeutic effects on ALI, yet its underlying molecular mechanism remains elusive. Core ALI target genes were identified and screened via the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), differential analysis, and machine learning. Baicalin target genes were obtained using Super-PRED, the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database (CTD), and SwissTargetPrediction, with Cytoscape 3.9.1 employed for network construction. H1N1 was used to induce in vivo and in vitro ALI models. Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8), reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), cell transfection, western blot (WB), and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) detected cell viability, mRNA levels, gene overexpression, protein levels, and inflammatory cytokines. Transepithelial electrical resistance (TER) and Transwell assays assessed transmembrane resistance and monolayer permeability, while hematoxylin-eosin (HE) staining, colorimetric assay, and bicinchoninic acid (BCA) assay evaluated tissue pathology, myeloperoxidase (MPO) activity, and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) protein concentration. Molecular docking and cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) were used to predict and evaluate the binding stability between proteins and small-molecule compounds. Integrated analyses revealed signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 (STAT1) as the potential key target of baicalin against H1N1-induced ALI. In cell models, H1N1 elevated IL-1beta, IL-6, and CXCL10 levels, reduced TER, increased monolayer permeability, and downregulated ZO-1 and Claudin-5; baicalin partially reversed these changes, whereas STAT1 overexpression attenuated baicalin's effects. Animal models confirmed H1N1-induced lung damage, increased lung wet/dry (W/D) ratio, elevated MPO activity and BALF protein concentration, validating the regulatory roles of H1N1, baicalin, and STAT1 overexpression. Baicalin alleviates H1N1-induced ALI progression by regulating STAT1, suggesting a possible therapeutic mechanism in ALI.
abstract_zh: 血凝素1神经氨酸酶1（H1N1）感染会引发急性肺损伤（ALI），而黄芩苷对ALI具有治疗作用，但其潜在分子机制仍不明确。通过基因表达综合数据库（GEO）、加权基因共表达网络分析（WGCNA）、差异分析及机器学习，识别并筛选出核心ALI靶基因。利用Super-PRED、比较毒物基因组学数据库（CTD）和SwissTargetPrediction获取黄芩苷靶基因，并采用Cytoscape 3.9.1进行网络构建。使用H1N1诱导体内和体外ALI模型。通过细胞计数试剂盒-8（CCK-8）、逆转录定量聚合酶链反应（RT-qPCR）、细胞转染、蛋白质印迹（WB）和酶联免疫吸附测定（ELISA）检测细胞活力、mRNA水平、基因过表达、蛋白水平和炎症细胞因子。跨上皮电阻（TER）和Transwell实验评估跨膜电阻和单层通透性，而苏木精-伊红（HE）染色、比色法和二喹啉甲酸（BCA）法评估组织病理、髓过氧化物酶（MPO）活性和支气管肺泡灌洗液（BALF）蛋白浓度。分子对接和细胞热位移分析（CETSA）用于预测和评估蛋白质与小分子化合物之间的结合稳定性。综合分析揭示信号转导与转录激活因子1（STAT1）是黄芩苷对抗H1N1诱导ALI的潜在关键靶点。在细胞模型中，H1N1升高IL-1β、IL-6和CXCL10水平，降低TER，增加单层通透性，并下调ZO-1和Claudin-5；黄芩苷部分逆转了这些变化，而STAT1过表达减弱了黄芩苷的作用。动物模型证实H1N1诱导的肺损伤、肺湿/干（W/D）比增加、MPO活性和BALF蛋白浓度升高，验证了H1N1、黄芩苷和STAT1过表达的调控作用。黄芩苷通过调控STAT1缓解H1N1诱导的ALI进展，提示其在ALI中可能的治疗机制。
